thread:
maya: RFC follow-up: continuous-batcher refactor. do we go full orchestration or hybrid?
dan: hybrid imo. keep local admission fast but centralize deadline/fallback policy.
ross: agree. main concern is debugging causal chains when decisions are split. we need traceability.
taru: propose lightweight admission token that flows on the bus (trace_id, tenant, length, deadline, qos). runtime keeps full request.
maya: agreed. log tokens async to event sink (kafka) with host seq# for ordering. consumer will materialize traces for obs.
dan: fallback behavior: if signals are missing, local runtime does pessimistic fallback at min(rem_deadline/3,50ms). conductor can override later.
ross: rollout: instrument dev cluster passive for 3w (emit but don't use), then 5% canary with smoke test suite comparing outputs. gate on p95 enqueue < +10% and fallback rate <2x.
maya: action items: @dan implement token proto + async logger, @ross build trace materializer, @taru add dashboards and smoke tests.
deploy-bot: Canary started: cb-refactor-hybrid on batch-dev-4 (canary id=cr-2026-04-23-1).
